column1: # The struct-field table: messages that no callee-based gate in this repository can see.
# A message written into a struct field — `&RunError{Msg: fmt.Sprintf("...", x)}` — is not an argument
# to anything, so the coverage scanner (which reads literals passed to `msg`, `T`, `warn`, `errf`,
# `replyErr`) never sees it, the ratchets never count it, and the catalog's Chinese for it is never
# reached. docs/i18n-design.md 7.5 measures the surface: 94 distinct literals, 29 of which the shipped
# catalog already translates and 64 of which it does not.
# The rows are listed by the shape that hid them rather than by domain, because they are not one
# domain: the sites are in internal/lang/{eval,typecheck,vm,value}.go and their translations were
# written down under typecheck and compiler. Splitting them by owner now would put one message in two
# tables and reintroduce exactly the disagreement this migration removes.
# A row whose zh repeats its en is NOT a translation. It is the backlog: the message shipped
# English-only, no Chinese for it exists anywhere in this repository or in the pinned module, and
# inventing one would change what a reader sees. Those Chinese values have to come from a speaker, and
# TestProofUntranslatedFieldMessagesAreCounted freezes the count so it can only shrink.
# id     dotted <domain>.<snake_case>, stable forever, never renumbered, never recycled
# owner  "local": this repository owns the text
# ctx    the site the message was found at, for the translator
# note   what the message means, for the translator
# src    the text this repository ships; for a local id the generator requires it to repeat the source
